summary: Read-only review complete. Ten findings remain in ceremony authorization, recovery, admission, throttling, and feature gating. No edits, builds, tests, network access, or .env reads performed.

findings.title: Admin registration can outlive session revocation
findings.detail: Registration verifies requireStepUp at admission and later checks only TOTP under the admin row lock. A request admitted before a concurrent password change can resume after that change revoked its session and still insert a permanent passkey: matching challenge.session_hash does not establish session liveness. packages/api/src/routes/admin-helpers.ts:50 caches the principal and :124 checks its in-memory stepUpAt; packages/api/src/auth/admin-session.ts:94 revokes competing sessions. The existing factor mutation explicitly rechecks and locks the live session at packages/api/src/auth/admin-staff.ts:74.
findings.fix: Require authenticated admin ceremonies to lock and revalidate the owning session, expiry, idle timeout, and required step-up freshness inside the mutation transaction. Add a registration-versus-password-change/session-revocation control.

findings.title: Credential-first locking deadlocks with customer recovery
findings.detail: Login locks the passkey credential before creating a session. Recovery takes the customer FOR UPDATE first and will then delete passkeys. Login can hold the credential while waiting for the customer FK lock during session insertion, while recovery holds the customer and waits for that credential. The existing ordering is explicit in packages/api/src/routes/customer-tokens.ts:129 and packages/api/src/routes/auth.ts:163; session creation inserts at packages/api/src/auth/session.ts:74 and its customer FK exists in packages/api/drizzle/0009_model_completeness.sql:114. Counter serialization alone does not resolve this cycle.
findings.fix: Specify one owner-first lock order across login, management, recovery, and credential deletion. Use an unlocked lookup only to identify the owner, then lock the owner and revalidate the challenge and credential. Exercise both race orderings against PostgreSQL.

findings.title: Image rollback can resurrect credentials invalidated by recovery
findings.detail: Retaining rows and automatically restoring enrollments after running the previous image breaks the new recovery guarantees. The previous password-reset implementation changes the password and revokes sessions but cannot delete passkeys (packages/api/src/routes/customer-tokens.ts:128). A malicious passkey therefore survives recovery performed during rollback and works again after re-upgrade. Similarly, the previous image permits TOTP disable under optional policy and deletes recovery codes without checking retained passkeys (packages/api/src/auth/admin-staff.ts:82).
findings.fix: Define a rollback-compatible invalidation mechanism or require a compatibility image that preserves passkey recovery and TOTP invariants. Rehearse password recovery and TOTP disable during downgrade, then verify affected credentials remain invalid after re-upgrade.

findings.title: Per-credential throttling borrows another connection while holding transaction locks
findings.detail: Section 5 places credential lookup inside the ceremony transaction; this paragraph requires consume after that lookup. The PostgreSQL limiter opens another connection from the same pool at packages/api/src/auth/rate-limit-backend.ts:129. Concurrent verifications can occupy every connection with ceremony transactions and then wait for additional connections, starving the API until connection timeouts. packages/api/src/routes/customer-tokens.ts:221 explicitly keeps limiter calls outside withStore for this reason.
findings.fix: Reserve credential budgets before opening the ceremony transaction, with any required preliminary lookup followed by authoritative revalidation inside it, or provide a transaction-aware limiter with explicit failure-count persistence. Add bounded-pool concurrency coverage using the PostgreSQL backend.

findings.title: Single-use fresh proof cannot authorize both registration requests
findings.detail: Both register/options and register/verify require fresh proof, while passkey and mailbox proofs are single-use. Consuming proof at options makes the same proof fail at verify; postponing consumption is not specified. Additionally, section 5 assigns credential deletion to every manage ceremony, although manage assertions also authorize adding credentials. Existing consumers actually burn proofs transactionally: packages/api/src/auth/magic-link.ts:71 and packages/api/src/auth/federated-link.ts:110. There is no reusable management authorization supplied by those helpers.
findings.fix: Define the complete add/remove state machine. Either consume proof once to mint a short-lived authorization bound to the registration challenge, session, browser, and operation, or require proof only at the final mutation. Separate manage-proof verification from the deletion effect and test complete flows for every proof type.

findings.title: Mailbox management proof lacks its schema and issuance route
findings.detail: The proposed passkey_manage customer_token kind is rejected by the existing database CHECK in packages/api/drizzle/0061_passwordless_signin.sql:17 and is absent from the Drizzle enum at packages/api/src/db/schema-content.ts:25. The supplied migration never widens that constraint. The route table also provides no mailbox-proof issuance endpoint; manage/options specifically requires an existing passkey. Passwordless Google/Apple customers therefore lack the promised first-passkey enrollment flow.
findings.fix: Add the additive CHECK and enum changes, and specify a session-authenticated, rate-limited mailbox-proof issuance route with transactional outbox delivery, browser/session binding, redemption, and matrix coverage.

findings.title: Passkey login bypasses the existing verified-email requirement
findings.detail: Registration already issues a customer session while emailVerified is false (packages/api/src/routes/auth.ts:117). That customer can satisfy the proposed password fresh proof and enroll a passkey without proving the mailbox. The proposed passkey login then creates sessions without checking emailVerified, bypassing the explicit native-login refusal at packages/api/src/routes/auth.ts:177. The design's assumption that an existing account has already established mailbox ownership is false.
findings.fix: Require verified email before customer passkey enrollment and authentication, or explicitly define an equally restrictive unverified-account flow. Test real signup followed by passkey enrollment/login before and after email verification; never treat a WebAuthn assertion as mailbox proof.

findings.title: SERVICE_CREDENTIAL_ROUTES does not enforce the claimed principal outcomes
findings.detail: This exemption lets unresolved bearer credentials reach the handler; it does not deny release-service or cache credentials. packages/api/src/routes/admin-agent-guard.ts:56 passes unresolved credentials through exempt routes, and only resolved agents reach its deny set. The actual staff/accept matrix explicitly allows release_service and cache_token at packages/api/src/sdk/authorization-matrix.identity-cases.testkit.ts:33, contradicting section 8. A valid enrollment-only human cookie also still triggers the enrollment guard at admin-agent-guard.ts:73, contradicting the claim that valid cookies are ignored.
findings.fix: Specify an explicit pre-session principal policy and implement it at the guard/handler boundary. Align matrix outcomes with that policy and cover absent, stale, valid, enrollment-only, agent, release-service, and cache credentials separately.

findings.title: Shop limiter permits only four complete logins per shared IP
findings.detail: attemptRetryAfter uses a single ip|identifier bucket capped at eight attempts per fifteen minutes (packages/api/src/auth/rate-limit.ts:19 and :32). Giving every shopper in a store the identifier passkey:storeId and consuming it for both options and verify permits only four successful ceremonies per shared IP. Autofill starts and canceled prompts consume the same budget, so a few page loads can block every shopper behind that NAT.
findings.fix: Use an explicitly sized subjectless store/IP admission budget and a separate credential budget. Specify how options, canceled autofill, and successful verification affect capacity, and test multiple legitimate customers sharing one peer.

findings.title: Feature flag cannot gate either public sign-in UI through admin/me
findings.detail: The only advertised capability response is authenticated GET /v1/admin/me, which anonymous admin login cannot access (packages/api/src/routes/admin.ts:124). Storefront customers cannot access it either. Their existing public capability endpoint exposes only auth.magicLink at packages/api/src/routes/shop-config.ts:42, consumed by packages/storefront/src/routes/sign-in/index.tsx:59. Consequently PASSKEYS_ENABLED=0 does not provide the specified mechanism for hiding public passkey buttons or stopping autofill requests.
findings.fix: Expose the capability through appropriate public admin and store-scoped storefront configuration, defaulting to disabled when absent or unavailable. Cover disabled-server and previous-image responses with both newer clients, including conditional authentication startup.
